selector_contract: Exact case-sensitive cache_metadata.parts[].name; numerical indices are documentation only and never selector identity. No selector is invented for spaces, omitted vessels or nerves.
presentation: Manual steps reuse existing supported camera and hidden-part metadata. Function is explained by states/captions; no geometry animation is fabricated.
scale_note: Gross specimens: 1 unit ≈ 6 cm (caecum ≈ 7.5 cm wide, anal canal ≈ 4 cm long). Wall coats are drawn about 1.5× their true thickness so each layer reads in section.

sources.title: Kumar & Phillips: contribution of external ligamentous attachments to function of the ileocecal junction (1987)
sources.evidence_scope: Primary experiment; human autopsy specimens and dogs. External geometry contributed to reflux competence. Its experimental pressures are not patient thresholds or animation parameters.

sources.title: StatPearls: Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis: Appendix (updated August 2023)
sources.evidence_scope: Mucosal/submucosal lymphoid tissue; appendicular supply and ileocolic lymphatic context; variable appendix tip. Immune role and microbiota safe-house hypothesis must not be treated as a demonstrated animated process.

sources.title: StatPearls: Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis: Anal Canal (updated May 2023)
sources.evidence_scope: RAIR, IAS/EAS behavior; above/below pectinate-line sensation and regional drainage. Regional routes have overlap.

sources.title: StatPearls: Physiology, Defecation (updated November 2023)
sources.evidence_scope: Rectal filling, enteric reflex, voluntary deferral, coordinated pelvic-muscle relaxation and propulsion. No quantified timing is transferred to this specimen.

sources.title: StatPearls: Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis, Rectum (updated July 2023)
sources.evidence_scope: Rectal circular/longitudinal muscle relationships, superior versus pelvic vascular routes, and superior rectal/inferior mesenteric plus internal iliac lymphatic drainage.

sources.title: Raizada & Mittal: Pelvic floor anatomy and applied physiology (2008)
sources.evidence_scope: Puborectalis and anorectal-angle mechanism; muscle nomenclature/three-part EAS representation is debated. Avoid treating legacy EAS parts as three separate perfect functional rings.

sources.title: Johns Hopkins Medicine: Hemorrhoids
sources.evidence_scope: Normal anal cushions include vascular and nonvascular components and contribute to continence; swelling/irritation indicates hemorrhoidal disease.

sequences.title: Ileocaecal transit
sequences.mechanism: Trace the anatomical route from terminal ileum through the junction into caecum; explain the distinction between passage anatomy and reflux competence.

steps.caption: Locate terminal ileum and its mucosa approaching the caecal wall.
The upper and lower lips and their frenula frame the ileal orifice. This is folded bowel tissue in wall context.
Teaching route: terminal ileum → junction → caecal cavity. A visible slit alone does not establish a continuous open lumen.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: Reflux competence depends on more than lip appearance; omitted attachment geometry and living muscle behavior cannot be tested in this static opened specimen.

schematic_limitations: Manual ordered selection and captions only; no bolus collision, valve deformation, flow velocity, pressure or competence simulation.
Separate-machine lumen tracing must verify ileum–orifice–caecum before any stronger patency statement.
Do not animate two lips as a rigid hinge, airtight seal or fully characterized muscular sphincter.
Caecal window and specimen cuts are intentional exposure, not leakage or physiological openings.

sequences.title: Appendix wall and supply
sequences.mechanism: Locate appendiceal lymphoid tissue in its bowel-wall context, then locate supply in mesoappendix.

steps.caption: Follow the converging taeniae to the appendix base; this model shows one representative appendix position.
Lymphoid tissue belongs in mucosa and submucosa beneath the exposed luminal surface. It is not a set of free luminal particles.
These enlarged representative follicles provide immune wall context. Cell trafficking, antibody production and microbiota reseeding are not depicted.
Keep mesoappendix visible as the contextual carrier of appendicular supply.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.
No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

schematic_limitations: Gross teaching scale, not counted follicles, cell populations or histological magnification.
Immune function is contextual; do not animate antigen sampling or present safe-house hypothesis as demonstrated behavior.
Appendicular venous drainage is not represented by an existing selector.

Diagram routes do not assert a single universal arterial branch pattern. The full wall and mesoappendix must remain in view; bead-like lumen ownership remains a geometry failure until corrected and reviewed.

sequences.title: Rectoanal coordination
sequences.mechanism: Distinguish rectal filling and IAS inhibition from voluntary outlet relaxation and coordinated evacuation.

steps.caption: The rectal ampulla acts as a temporary reservoir. Filling distends the rectal wall; folds remain anatomical landmarks.
At rest, IAS tone, the EAS complex and puborectalis support continence. The IAS continues from rectal circular smooth muscle.
Rectal distension triggers the rectoanal inhibitory reflex: IAS relaxation. This reflex alone does not mean defecation occurs.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: When defecation is deferred, voluntary EAS contraction maintains the outlet barrier. The puborectalis sling supports the anorectal bend.
For evacuation, outlet relaxation is coordinated with propulsive force. Puborectalis relaxation allows the anorectal angle to widen.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: Return to resting continence as outlet muscles resume tone; this state is a qualitative teaching summary, not a timed physiological measurement.

schematic_limitations: No dynamic deformation, manometry, patient-specific angle, timing, pressure, nerve geometry or stool model is supplied.
All three existing EAS selectors are retained and taught as one complex. Their boundaries and classification vary across anatomical accounts.
Anorectal widening is explained by a caption; no displacement of a disconnected levator slab is accepted as proof of function.
The model omits bony origins, perineal body, coccygeal attachments and other pelvic viscera. It cannot show a complete pelvic-floor action map.
A diagnosis of dyssynergia, incontinence or sphincter injury cannot be inferred from this schematic.

sequences.title: Rectal arterial routes
sequences.mechanism: Keep arterial supply distinct from venous return; identify represented superior rectal branches and omitted pelvic contribution.

steps.caption: Arterial inflow: inferior mesenteric artery → superior rectal artery → rectal wall. The proximal origin and terminal microvessels are omitted.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: Middle and inferior rectal arteries contribute to distal territories; they are not present as named vessel meshes. Territories overlap.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.
No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

schematic_limitations: No artery-to-vein connecting tube may be added to make a route look continuous.
Displayed ends are cut/omitted continuations; branch topology, perfused territory and capillary patency need separate validation.
Maintain mesorectal and wall context even when selected vessels are emphasized.

sequences.title: Rectal venous routes
sequences.mechanism: Separate portal-dominant superior drainage from omitted systemic routes; explain normal cushions without conflating disease.

steps.caption: The named internal plexus represents only the vascular component of normal anal cushions; normal cushions also contain supporting nonvascular tissue.
Superior route: rectal venous network → superior rectal vein → inferior mesenteric vein → portal circulation. Omitted links are diagram annotations.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: Distal venous return also reaches systemic circulation through pelvic veins. Portal–systemic communications are not explicitly reconstructed.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: Normal cushions, symptomatic hemorrhoidal disease and anorectal varices are different concepts. Purple shape alone depicts none of their clinical diagnoses.

schematic_limitations: Disconnected displayed venous pieces do not establish drainage continuity. Do not invent a direct artery-to-vein bridge.
No disease animation, reflux direction, congestion severity, thrombosis, prolapse or variceal collateral is represented.
Regional drainage is a simplified route explanation with overlap; pectinate line is not an impermeable vascular border.

sequences.title: Regional lymphatic routes
sequences.mechanism: Keep mesorectal nodes in fat/wall context and explain the regional continuations beyond the model.

steps.caption: Mesorectal nodes belong to the mesorectal compartment; they must remain contextualized rather than floating isolated dots.
A superior route continues through superior rectal lymphatics toward inferior mesenteric nodes, beyond this model.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: Additional rectal drainage reaches internal iliac nodes. Avoid teaching all tissue above the pectinate line as an exclusive mesorectal pathway.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

steps.caption: Below the pectinate line, superficial inguinal drainage is the key regional route; these nodes and channels are omitted.

schematic_annotations.geometry_claim: No 3D connection or vessel lumen is implied.

schematic_limitations: No explicit lymphatic vessel meshes, flow rates, complete nodal counts or cancer spread simulation are supplied.
Routes overlap and vary; representative node dots do not specify every drainage basin.
Pectinate line is a landmark for regional teaching, not a watertight lymphatic partition.
